evidence.method: Manual boundary transcription checked against the published score; no automated score parsing.

entries.label: S3
entries.notes: Stanza at P19; the closing G3 belongs to the lower strand of the P26 double stop.

evidence.method: Manual boundary transcription checked against the published score; no automated score parsing.

entries.label: S4
entries.notes: Return at P27, Molto tranquillo; the melodic B4 at P34 beat 2 supplies the endpoint.

evidence.method: Manual boundary transcription checked against the published score; no automated score parsing.

entries.label: D1
entries.notes: First dux. The full final quarter note of C8 is included.

evidence.method: Manual boundary transcription checked against the published score; no automated score parsing.

entries.label: C1
entries.notes: First comes: enters one quarter after D1. The melody continues in the lower strand near its ending, through C9 beat 1.

evidence.method: Manual boundary transcription checked against the published score; no automated score parsing.

entries.label: D2
entries.notes: Second dux begins at C9 and ends after C16 beat 2.

evidence.method: Manual boundary transcription checked against the published score; no automated score parsing.

entries.label: C2
entries.notes: Second comes: enters two quarters after D2, at C10; its final quarter releases after C17 beat 2.

evidence.method: Manual boundary transcription checked against the published score; no automated score parsing.

entries.label: D3
entries.notes: Third dux has altered continuation. Its last E4 at C24 beat 2 is tied through C25 beat 1; the transition starts at C25 beat 2.

entries.notes: Third comes: enters three quarters after D3, at C18 beat 2. Its altered tail ends with the full B3 quarter at C25 beat 2.

analysis.description: Selected melodic statements: four prelude stanzas and the dux/comes pairs of all three opening canons, manually checked against the final published score and Nakahara’s analysis. The altered prelude coda, accompanying counterpoint and later Canon development are unclassified. Both colors denote settings of the same folk tune.

notes: Selected melodic statements: four prelude stanzas and the dux/comes pairs of all three opening canons, manually checked against the final published score and Nakahara’s analysis. The altered prelude coda, accompanying counterpoint and later Canon development are unclassified. Both colors denote settings of the same folk tune.

P1–P48 and C1–C47 count the Prelude and Canon separately. The consulted edition has no printed bar numbers; these are editorial counts checked against its barlines. All bars are 2/4. Quarter zero is the first attack of the Prelude; the Canon begins at quarter 96.

S1–S4 are the four selected prelude stanzas. D1/C1, D2/C2 and D3/C3 denote the dux/comes pairs, not separate folk tunes. Dux entries start on E5; the three comes entries begin on G4, A4 and B4, delayed by one, two and three quarters respectively.

Entry endpoints include the final written releases and ties. The third canon is altered: its dux spans 17 quarters including the tie into C25; its comes spans 15 quarters and closes at the end of C25. Neither is forced into the 16-quarter template of the earlier statements.

The fifth prelude stanza/coda from P35 has a shortened/altered opening. Nakahara’s Table 1 gives its notional B-register identity, but the published Violin II line actually enters on a sustained F-sharp. It is left unclassified here. Later fragments and development after the third canon are also unclassified; blank areas do not imply silence.

Nakahara discusses draft revisions as well as the final work. Only the published edition supplies the coordinates and incipit notes used here. The article provides the thematic and canonic interpretation, not an encoded occurrence inventory.

The two preview colors distinguish Prelude and Canon settings of the same Hungarian folk tune, Két szál pünkösdrózsa. Previews isolate six melodic notes; they are not full textures and do not change pitch with the selected entry.
The recording covers the complete duo. Manual timing is still needed; no tempo-derived or borrowed synchronization has been added.
